plain_english: The supplied page is Andrew Glasgow's testament-testamentar and inventory. The ScotlandsPeople index confirms Corstoun in the parish of Caldercleir, sheriffdom of Edinburgh; the manuscript's residence strokes remain provisionally read as Corsoun. It records his death on 7 February and says that he gave up the inventory himself on 6 February. The latter-will opening at the bottom expressly bears 6 February 1597 as written.

The inventory includes cows with calves, young cattle, horses, sheep, oats, barley, household furnishings and clothing. Incoming and outgoing accounts name financial associates, but their appearance here does not establish family relationships.

The continuation freshly confirms Elizat Stevinsoun as Andrew's spouse and Robert Glasgow as his son begotten upon Elizat his wife. It names daughters Marione, Jonet and Isobell in the alternative distribution, provides for a possible unborn child only conditionally, and directs that Elizat retain the land or holding until Robert came of age.
findings: Image 123, lines 4-9: this is a testament-testamentar, distinct from a testament-dative. The decedent's own act on the sixth and death on the seventh are legible; uncertain year numerals in the opening should be checked against the clearer 1597 at the latter-will opening.

Image 123, line 42: 6 February 1597 is the written latter-will date. The existing record describes this as 1597/8 under the pre-1600 Scottish year convention; that is a dating interpretation, not a different date written on the image.
Image 123, lines 24-36: financial associates and possible Stevenson names are not described here as Andrew's parents, children or siblings.
Image 124, family clause: 'Elizat stevinsoun his spous' and 'Robart glasgw his sone begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff' directly establish Andrew and Elizat as Robert's parents.
Image 124, distribution: Marione, Jonet and Isobell are named after wording identifying Andrew's daughters; Elizat is not expressly called their mother in this clause.

Image 124, contingency and succession: a possible child in utero is conditional, not evidence of a birth, while Robert had not yet reached the stated age and was intended to succeed to Andrew's land or holding.
Image 124 record boundary: Andrew's entry ends before the separate lower testament; no names from that next entry are assigned to his family.
changes_from_previous: Closes the false continuation gap by freshly reading image 124 from the nested PDF and supplied PNGs; coverage is now full for the two-image record span.
Freshly supports the testament type, Caldercleir setting, sixth/seventh-February sequence and the written 1597 latter-will date.
Freshly confirms rather than merely carrying forward Elizat Stevinsoun, Robert, and daughters Marione, Jonet and Isobell from the older continuation review.
Keeps the unborn-child provision conditional and separates Robert's explicit maternity from the daughters' unstated maternity.
The outgoing Stevenson name may be patrik rather than James in one entry. The present reading is too uncertain for an identity correction; retain a flagged financial-name query.
unresolved: The indexed residence is confirmed as Corstoun; its individual manuscript strokes, witnesses, creditor names and most account numerals remain unresolved.
The outgoing Stevenson name requires comparison with a clearer same-hand example; no genealogical conclusion should depend on it.
The exact land or tenure term, adviser localities, and much of the closing formula on image 124 remain unresolved.
confidence_statement: Fresh visual review of both images and enlarged crops, with the earlier saved account consulted afterwards. High confidence in document type, written will date, Elizat as spouse, Robert's explicit parentage, the three daughter names, conditional unborn-child wording and record boundary; moderate confidence in the land-succession sense; low confidence in many financial names, sums, localities and legal formula. Full coverage describes the supplied span, not a complete diplomatic transcript.
